synopsis: Chapter 4 cites a 2025 IIHS study by Cox, Reagan and Cicchino finding that on-road drivers keep prevention systems enabled more often than warning-only systems [f3460]. In that study, 93% had AEB enabled, while lane departure systems were enabled less often; the stated scope is on-road drivers, not heavy off-road operators [f3461]. Chapter 12 cites Cox (2008) for mathematical flaws in colour risk matrices, including 5-by-5 heat maps: poor resolution, range compression and ranking errors [f9675, f9895]. Subsequent work is reported to confirm problems with ordinal scoring in risk matrices [f9676]. The supplied facts do not establish whether the Cox cited in these two research areas is the same person [f3460, f9675].

relations.note: Adds the 93% AEB-enabled figure and comparison with lane departure systems.
Both attribute risk heat-map ranking defects to Cox (2008); f9675 lists additional flaws.
Subsequent research confirms ordinal-scoring problems consistent with the earlier risk-matrix critique.
